legend: After learning the basics of matrices, Derar wants to learn the newest matrix algorithm "Matrix Bel Lotus."
Ahmad, its author, gave Derar n%%ZSMJ0%% videos. Video i%%ZSMJ1%% is di%%ZSMJ2%% minutes long.
Derar has T%%ZSMJ3%% minutes before the contest, and he has to watch all the videos. He can't skip a video, but he can watch video i%%ZSMJ4%% with any of the following speeds:
X1%%ZSMJ5%% speed: he will need di%%ZSMJ6%% minutes and will get 100%%ZSMJ7%% skill points.
X1.5%%ZSMJ8%% speed: he will need di1.5%%ZSMJ9%% minutes and will get 75%%ZSMJ10%% skill points.
X2%%ZSMJ11%% speed: he will need di2%%ZSMJ12%% minutes and will get 50%%ZSMJ13%% skill points.

It is guaranteed that di%%ZSMJ14%% is a multiple of 6%%ZSMJ15%%. So it can be proven that all the values in the problem are integers. And it is guaranteed that Derar can watch all the videos if he plays them at speed X2%%ZSMJ16%%.
You have to help Derar choose the speed of each video so he can watch all the videos in at most T%%ZSMJ17%% minutes and maximize the total sum of skill points.
input: The first line contains a single integer tc(1≤tc≤100)%%ZSMJ18%% — the number of testcases.
The first line of each testcase consists of two integers n,T(1≤n≤2⋅105)(1≤T≤1010)%%ZSMJ19%% — the number of videos and the number of minutes Derar has before the contest.
The second line of each testcase consists of n%%ZSMJ20%% integers di(1≤di≤1010)%%ZSMJ21%% — the duration of each video. It is guaranteed that di%%ZSMJ22%% is a multiple of 6%%ZSMJ23%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ24%% over all testcases doesn't exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ25%% , and Derar can watch all the videos if he plays them at speed X2%%ZSMJ26%%.
output: The output of each testcase consists of two lines:
On the first line, print the maximum sum of skill points Derar can achieve.
On the second line, print n%%ZSMJ27%% values, the speed he will watch each video with. The values should be 1,1.5%%ZSMJ28%% or 2%%ZSMJ29%%.
If there are multiple solutions, print any.
